sentences.text: Respondent No.2 herein had filed P.C.R.No.417/2023 before the Court of VIII ACMM, Bengaluru and learned Magistrate by order dated 13.01.2023 had referred the said complaint to the jurisdictional Police, who in turn had registered FIR in NC: 2024:KHC:15166 Crime No.16/2023 for the aforesaid offences against the petitioners herein and 20 others.
The petitioners are arrayed as accused nos.1 to 3 in the FIR.

Crl .P.No.2365/2023 is filed by accused no.3, who is the brother of accused No.2 defacto complainant and Crl.P.No.2917/2023 is filed by accused Nos.1 and 2 who are the parents of respondent no.2 and accused No.3.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature.
The allegation in the private complaint is about partition of joint family property.
The grievance of respondent no.2 is that he has been denied share in the family property.

He submits the respondent No.2 has already filed suit in O.S.No.224/2023 before the jurisdictional civil Court at Hyderabad as against the petitioners and other accused in the present case seeking for a decree of partition and separate possession of ancestral and joint family properties.

He submits that even if the allegations made in the private complaint are presumed to be true, the alleged NC:
2024:KHC:15166 offences do not get attracted against the petitioners.
Respondent No.2-defacto complainant prior to filling the private complaint had approached the police alleging that he was denied share in the ancestral property.
However, the police had refused to entertain the complaint since the dispute was civil in nature.

He submits that learned Magistrate without appreciating the contents of private complaint has mechanically referred the complaint under section 156(3) of Cr.P.C, which has now resulted in registration of criminal case as against the petitioners.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per Contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

6. From a perusal of the averments made in the private complaint, which has now resulted in registration of FIR in crime No.16/2023 as against the petitioners and other accused for the aforesaid offences it is seen that respondent No.2 is the son of accused No.1 and 2 and the brother of accused No.3.
The grievance of respondent NC: 2024:KHC:15166 No.2 in the complaint appears to be that he has denied his rightful share in the ancestral property of the family.

He has alleged in the complaint that he has got a reasonable suspicion that accused Nos.1 and 2 have purchased properties in their names from the rental income and sale proceedings of ancestral property without his knowledge.

He has referred to various sale transactions in his private complaint and his allegations are that sale proceedings derived from the aforesaid transactions have been utilized by accused persons for purchasing property in their names.
7.
From a perusal of entire averments made in the private complaint, it is very clear that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature.
By giving a criminal texture to the dispute which is otherwise civil in nature, criminal proceedings cannot be initiated.

As rightly contended by learned counsel for the petitioners even if the allegations made in the private complaint are presumed to be true, the alleged offences do not prima NC: 2024:KHC:15166 facie get attracted against the petitioners, who are family members of respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 has already filed a suit Dr. D. Satyanarayana vs State Of Karnataka on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116064013/
4 in O.S.No.224/2023 before the jurisdiction civil Court at Hyderabad as against the petitioners and other accused, seeking decree of partition and separate possession of the ancestral property and also properties subsequently purchased by accused persons which according to respondent No.2 is from the rental income and sale proceedings of ancestral property.

entities.text: Dr. D. Satyanarayana vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 who has already initiated civil proceedings with regard to his grievance which is made in the private complaint cannot be permitted to parallelly continue criminal proceedings on the very same grievance.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the impugned proceedings as against the petitioners is required to be quashed.
8. Accordingly, the petitions are allowed.

The entire proceedings in crime No.16/2023 registered by J.C. Nagar police station, Bengaluru for the NC: 2024:KHC:15166 offences punishable under sections 506, 120B, 384, 420, 447, 448, 465, 468, 471, 426 of IPC and the order dated 13.01.2023 passed in P.C.R.No.417/2023 pending before the Court of VIII ACMM, Bengaluru are hereby quashed.
